Result&lt;Arc&lt;prost_types::Any&gt;&gt; {\n    let uuid = index.uuid.to_string();\n    let type_key = crate::session::index_caches::ScalarIndexDetailsKey { uuid: &amp;uuid };\n    if let Some(index_details) = dataset.index_cache.get_with_key(&amp;type_key).await {\n        return Ok(index_details.0.clone());\n    }\n\n    let index_dir = dataset.indice_files_dir(index)?.child(uuid.clone());\n    let col = dataset.schema().field(column).ok_or(Error::Internal {\n        message: format!(\n            \"Index refers to column {} which does not exist in dataset schema\",\n            column\n        ),\n        location: location!(),\n    })?;\n\n    let bitmap_page_lookup = index_dir.child(BITMAP_LOOKUP_NAME);\n    let inverted_list_lookup = index_dir.child(METADATA_FILE);\n    let legacy_inverted_list_lookup = index_dir.child(INVERT_LIST_FILE);\n    let index_details = if let DataType::List(_) = col.data_type() {\n        prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;LabelListIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n    } else if dataset.object_store.exists(&amp;bitmap_page_lookup).await? {\n        prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;BitmapIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n    } else if dataset.object_store.exists(&amp;inverted_list_lookup).await? {\n        // Try to infer inverted index details from metadata file to capture with_position and other params\n        // Fall back to defaults if anything goes wrong\n        let default_details = prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;InvertedIndexDetails::default()).unwrap();\n        let parse_params = async || {\n            let index_store = LanceIndexStore::from_dataset_for_existing(dataset, index).ok()?;\n            let reader = index_store.open_index_file(METADATA_FILE).await.ok()?;\n            let params_str = reader.schema().metadata.get(\"params\")?;\n            let params = ::serde_json::from_str::&lt;InvertedIndexParams&gt;(params_str).ok()?;\n            let details = InvertedIndexDetails::try_from(&amp;params).ok()?;\n            Some(prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;details).unwrap())\n        };\n        parse_params().await.unwrap_or(default_details)\n    } else if dataset\n        .object_store\n        .exists(&amp;legacy_inverted_list_lookup)\n        .await?\n    {\n        prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;InvertedIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n    } else {\n        prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;BTreeIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n    };\n\n    let index_details = Arc::new(index_details);\n    let prost_any = Arc::new(ProstAny(index_details.clone()));\n\n    dataset\n        .index_cache\n        .insert_with_key(&amp;type_key, prost_any)\n        .await;\n    Ok(index_details)\n}\n\npub fn index_matches_criteria(\n    index: &amp;IndexMetadata,\n    criteria: &amp;ScalarIndexCriteria,\n    field: &amp;Field,\n    has_multiple_indices: bool,\n    schema: &amp;lance_core::datatypes::Schema,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;bool&gt; {\n    if let Some(name) = &amp;criteria.has_name {\n        if &amp;index.name != name {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if let Some(for_column) = criteria.for_column {\n        if index.fields.len() != 1 {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        // Build the full field path for nested fields\n        let field_path = if let Some(ancestors) = schema.field_ancestry_by_id(field.id) {\n            let field_refs: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = ancestors.iter().map(|f| f.name.as_str()).collect();\n            lance_core::datatypes::format_field_path(&amp;field_refs)\n        } else {\n            field.name.clone()\n        };\n        if for_column != field_path {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n    }\n\n    let index_details = index.index_details.clone().map(IndexDetails);\n    let Some(index_details) = index_details else {\n        if has_multiple_indices {\n            return Err(Error::InvalidInput {\n                                source: format!(\n                                    \"An index {} on the field with id {} co-exists with other indices on the same column but was written with an older Lance version, and this is not supported.  Please retrain this index.\",\n                                    index.name,\n                                    index.fields.first().unwrap_or(&amp;0),\n                                ).into(),\n                                location: location!(),\n                            });\n        }\n\n        // If we don't have details then allow it for backwards compatibility\n        return Ok(true);\n    };\n\n    if index_details.is_vector() {\n        // This method is only for finding matching scalar indexes today so reject any vector indexes\n        return Ok(false);\n    }\n\n    if criteria.must_support_fts &amp;&amp; !index_details.supports_fts() {\n        return Ok(false);\n    }\n\n    // We should not use FTS / NGram indices for exact equality queries\n    // (i.e. merge insert with a join on the indexed column)\n    if criteria.must_support_exact_equality {\n        let plugin = index_details.get_plugin()?;\n        if !plugin.provides_exact_answer() {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(true)\n}\n\n/// Initialize a scalar index from a source dataset\npub async fn initialize_scalar_index(\n    target_dataset: &amp;mut Dataset,\n    source_dataset: &amp;Dataset,\n    source_index: &amp;IndexMetadata,\n    field_names: &amp;[&amp;str],\n) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    if field_names.is_empty() || field_names.len() &gt; 1 {\n        return Err(Error::Index {\n            message: format!(\"Unsupported fields for scalar index: {:?}\", field_names),\n            location: location!(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // Scalar indices currently support only single fields, use the first one\n    let column_name = field_names[0];\n\n    let source_scalar_index = source_dataset\n        .open_scalar_index(\n            column_name,\n            &amp;source_index.uuid.to_string(),\n            &amp;NoOpMetricsCollector,\n        )\n        .await?;\n\n    let params = source_scalar_index.derive_index_params()?;\n    let index_type = source_scalar_index.index_type();\n\n    // For Inverted index, we need to parse the params JSON and create InvertedIndexParams\n    if index_type == IndexType::Inverted {\n        // Extract the JSON string from ScalarIndexParams\n        let params_json = params.params.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| Error::Index {\n            message: \"Inverted index params missing\".to_string(),\n            location: location!(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Parse the JSON into InvertedIndexParams\n        let inverted_params: InvertedIndexParams = serde_json::from_str(params_json)?;\n\n        target_dataset\n            .create_index(\n                &amp;[column_name],\n                index_type,\n                Some(source_index.name.clone()),\n                &amp;inverted_params,\n                false,\n            )\n            .await?;\n    } else {\n        target_dataset\n            .create_index(\n                &amp;[column_name],\n                index_type,\n                Some(source_index.name.clone()),\n                &amp;params,\n                false,\n            )\n            .await?;\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use crate::utils::test::{DatagenExt, FragmentCount, FragmentRowCount};\n\n    use super::*;\n    use arrow::{\n        array::AsArray,\n        datatypes::{Int32Type, UInt64Type},\n    };\n    use arrow_schema::DataType;\n    use futures::TryStreamExt;\n    use lance_core::utils::tempfile::TempStrDir;\n    use lance_core::{datatypes::Field, utils::address::RowAddress};\n    use lance_datagen::array;\n    use lance_index::pbold::NGramIndexDetails;\n    use lance_index::IndexType;\n    use lance_table::format::pb::VectorIndexDetails;\n\n    fn make_index_metadata(\n        name: &amp;str,\n        field_id: i32,\n        index_type: Option&lt;IndexType&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; crate::index::IndexMetadata {\n        let index_details = index_type\n            .map(|index_type| match index_type {\n                IndexType::BTree =&gt; {\n                    prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;BTreeIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n                }\n                IndexType::Inverted =&gt; {\n                    prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;InvertedIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n                }\n                IndexType::NGram =&gt; {\n prost_types::Any::from_msg(&amp;VectorIndexDetails::default()).unwrap()\n                }\n                _ =&gt; {\n                    unimplemented!(\"unsupported index type: {}\", index_type)\n                }\n            })\n            .map(Arc::new);\n        crate::index::IndexMetadata {\n            uuid: uuid::Uuid::new_v4(),\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            fields: vec![field_id],\n            dataset_version: 1,\n            fragment_bitmap: None,\n            index_details,\n            index_version: 0,\n            created_at: None,\n            base_id: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_index_matches_criteria_vector_index() {\n        let index1 = make_index_metadata(\"vector_index\", 1, Some(IndexType::Vector));\n\n        let index_matches_criteria(&amp;index1, &amp;criteria, &amp;field, false, &amp;schema).unwrap();\n        assert!(!result);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_index_matches_criteria_scalar_index() {\n `try_into_batch()` is a convenience method that does `try_into_stream().try_collect().concat_batches()`.

Both tests pass. Summary:

## Summary

### Difference between `try_into_batch()` and `try_into_stream()`

1. **`try_into_stream()`**:
   - Returns a stream of `RecordBatch` objects (async iterator)
   - Can yield multiple batches (one per fragment)
   - Useful for incremental processing or when you need batches separately
   - Returns: `DatasetRecordBatchStream` (a stream)

2. **`try_into_batch()`**:
   - Returns a single concatenated `RecordBatch`
   - Internally calls `try_into_stream()`, collects all batches, and concatenates them
   - Convenient when you want all data in one batch
   - Returns: `RecordBatch` (a single batch)

**Implementation:**
```rust
pub async fn try_into_batch(&self) -> Result<RecordBatch> {
    let stream = self.try_into_stream().await?;
    let schema = stream.schema();
    let batches = stream.try_collect::<Vec<_>>().await?;
    Ok(concat_batches(&schema, &batches)?)
}
```

### Fix applied

Updated `test_zonemap_deletion_then_index` to use `try_into_batch()` instead of `try_into_stream().try_collect()`, simplifying the code:

**Before:**
```rust
let after_index: Vec<arrow_array::RecordBatch> = ds
    .scan()
    .filter("value")
    .unwrap()
    .try_into_stream()
    .await
    .unwrap()
    .try_collect()
    .await
    .unwrap();

let after_ids: Vec<u64> = after_index[0]
    .column_by_name("id")
    .unwrap()
    // ...
```

**After:**
```rust
let after_index = ds
    .scan()
    .filter("value")
    .unwrap()
    .try_into_batch()
    .await
    .unwrap();

let after_ids: Vec<u64> = after_index["id"]
    .as_any()
    // ...
```

The test now passes, and the code is simpler since `try_into_batch()` handles concatenation automatically.

All tests pass. Summary of the fix:

## Summary

Fixed the forward compatibility test failure by adding backward compatibility support for reading zonemap and bloomfilter indices created with Lance 0.36.0.

### Problem
The forward compatibility test failed because:
- We changed `fragment_id`, `zone_start`, and `zone_length` from `UInt64` to `UInt32` in the new code
- Old data (from 0.36.0) has these fields as `UInt64`
- The deserialization code only accepted `UInt32`, causing a failure when reading old data

### Solution
Added backward compatibility in both `zonemap.rs` and `bloomfilter.rs`:

1. Created a helper function `read_u32_array()` that:
   - First tries to read as `UInt32Array` (new format)
   - If that fails, tries `UInt64Array` (old format from 0.36.0)
   - Converts `UInt64` values to `UInt32` with bounds checking
   - Returns an error if the column is neither type

2. Updated deserialization to use this helper for:
   - `fragment_id`
   - `zone_start`
   - `zone_length`

### Files Modified
- `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/zonemap.rs`: Added backward compatibility in `try_from_serialized()`
- `rust/lance-index/src/scalar/bloomfilter.rs`: Added backward compatibility in `try_from_serialized()`

### Testing
- All existing tests pass
- The code compiles successfully
- The forward compatibility test should now pass when reading data from 0.36.0

The fix ensures that:
- New indices are written with `UInt32` (more efficient)
- Old indices written with `UInt64` can still be read correctly
- Values are validated to ensure they fit in `u32` when converting from `u64`

This maintains backward compatibility while using the more efficient `u32` type for new indices.

## Summary

Updated the code to match the new type changes in `BloomFilterStatistics` and `ZoneMapStatistics`:

### Type Changes:
- `fragment_id`: `u32` → `u64`
- `zone_start`: `u32` → `u64`
- `zone_length`: `u32` → `usize`

### Changes Made:

1. **Arrow Schema Definitions** (both files):
   - Changed `DataType::UInt32` → `DataType::UInt64` for `fragment_id`, `zone_start`, and `zone_length`

2. **Array Creation** (serialization):
   - Changed `UInt32Array::from_iter_values()` → `UInt64Array::from_iter_values()` for all three fields
   - Added `as u64` cast for `zone_length` when creating arrays (since it's `usize`)

3. **Array Deserialization**:
   - Changed `downcast_ref::<UInt32Array>()` → `downcast_ref::<UInt64Array>()` for all three fields
   - Added `as usize` cast when reading `zone_length` from arrays

4. **Builder Code**:
   - Updated `new_map()` and `new_block()` to cast `fragment_id` and `zone_start` to `u64`
   - Updated `zone_length` calculation to return `usize` directly

5. **Search/Query Code**:
   - Removed unnecessary `as u64` casts for `fragment_id` and `zone_start` (they're already `u64`)
   - Kept `as u64` cast for `zone_length` when calculating address ranges

6. **Fragment ID Insertion**:
   - Added `as u32` cast when inserting into `RoaringBitmap` (it expects `u32`)

7. **Test Assertions**:
   - Updated all test assertions to use `u64` for `fragment_id` and `zone_start`
   - `zone_length` assertions remain as `usize` (no change needed)

8. **Imports**:
   - Added `UInt64Array` to imports in both files
   - Removed unused `UInt32Array` import from bloomfilter

All tests pass. The code compiles and works with the new types.

## Simple Example: Stable Row IDs vs Row Addresses

### Initial State

```rust
// Dataset with 3 fragments
Fragment 0: [Alice, Bob, Charlie]     // 3 rows
Fragment 1: [David, Eve]               // 2 rows  
Fragment 2: [Frank, Grace, Henry]     // 3 rows

// Row IDs are assigned sequentially (stable identifiers)
Row ID 0 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 0) = Alice
Row ID 1 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 1) = Bob
Row ID 2 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 2) = Charlie
Row ID 3 -> Row Address (fragment: 1, offset: 0) = David
Row ID 4 -> Row Address (fragment: 1, offset: 1) = Eve
Row ID 5 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 0) = Frank
Row ID 6 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 1) = Grace
Row ID 7 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 2) = Henry
```

### After Deletions and Compaction

```rust
// Delete Bob (Row ID 1) and Eve (Row ID 4)
// After compaction, data is reorganized:

Fragment 0: [Alice, Charlie]          // Bob deleted
Fragment 1: [David]                   // Eve deleted
Fragment 2: [Frank, Grace, Henry]     // Unchanged

// Row IDs STAY THE SAME (stable!)
// But Row Addresses CHANGE (physical location changed)

Row ID 0 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 0) = Alice  ✅ Same
Row ID 1 -> DELETED                                    ❌ Gone
Row ID 2 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 1) = Charlie  ⚠️ Changed! (was offset: 2)
Row ID 3 -> Row Address (fragment: 1, offset: 0) = David  ✅ Same
Row ID 4 -> DELETED                                    ❌ Gone
Row ID 5 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 0) = Frank  ✅ Same
Row ID 6 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 1) = Grace  ✅ Same
Row ID 7 -> Row Address (fragment: 2, offset: 2) = Henry  ✅ Same
```

### Key Points:

1. Row ID (stable): Unique `u64` that doesn't change
   - Row ID 2 always refers to Charlie, even if the physical location changes

2. Row Address (can change): Physical location = `(fragment_id << 32) | local_offset`
   - After compaction, Charlie moves from `(0, 2)` to `(0, 1)`
   - The Row ID index maps Row ID → current Row Address

3. Why it matters:
   - External references can use Row IDs (stable)
   - Lance uses Row Addresses internally (efficient physical access)
   - The Row ID index keeps the mapping up to date

### Real-World Analogy:

- Row ID = Social Security Number (never changes)
- Row Address = Home Address (can change when you move)

You can always find someone by their SSN, but you need to look up their current address in a directory.

This is why Lance maintains a Row ID index: it maps stable Row IDs to their current Row Addresses, enabling efficient lookups even after data reorganization.

You're correct. The documentation states: "Deletion vectors are applied during filtering, not at the storage level."

## Corrected Example:

### Initial State
```rust
Fragment 0: [Alice, Bob, Charlie]     // Physical offsets: 0, 1, 2

Row ID 0 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 0) = Alice
Row ID 1 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 1) = Bob
Row ID 2 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 2) = Charlie
```

### After Deleting Bob (Row ID 1)
```rust
// Physical file STAYS THE SAME - deletion is tracked separately!
Fragment 0: [Alice, Bob, Charlie]     // Still at offsets: 0, 1, 2
Deletion vector: [offset 1]            // Marks Bob as deleted

// Row addresses DON'T CHANGE because physical file doesn't change
Row ID 0 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 0) = Alice  ✅ Same
Row ID 1 -> DELETED (still at offset 1, but filtered out)  ❌
Row ID 2 -> Row Address (fragment: 0, offset: 2) = Charlie  ✅ Still offset 2!
```

### Key Point:
- Deletions are tracked in deletion vectors/files, not by rewriting the data file
- Physical offsets remain unchanged until compaction
- During reads, deletion vectors filter out deleted rows
- Row addresses only change if compaction rewrites the fragment

So Charlie (Row ID 2) stays at offset 2 even after Bob is deleted. The deletion vector marks offset 1 as deleted, but the physical positions don't shift.

---

Recommended approach: extract a common struct and use composition.

## Solution: Extract Common Fields into a Shared Struct

Create a shared struct for the common fields:

```rust
// In rust/lance-index/src/scalar/mod.rs or a new common.rs file

/// Common zone/block metadata shared across scalar indices
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ZoneMetadata {
    /// Fragment ID containing this zone
    pub fragment_id: u64,
    /// Start row offset of the zone in the fragment (local offset)
    /// To get the actual first row address: `fragment_id << 32 + zone_start`
    pub zone_start: u64,
    /// Row offset span between the first and last row in the zone
    /// Calculated as: (last_row_offset - first_row_offset + 1)
    pub zone_length: usize,
}

impl ZoneMetadata {
    /// Calculate the full row address for the start of this zone
    pub fn start_row_address(&self) -> u64 {
        (self.fragment_id << 32) + self.zone_start
    }
    
    /// Calculate the full row address for the end of this zone (exclusive)
    pub fn end_row_address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start_row_address() + self.zone_length as u64
    }
}
```

Then use composition in both structs:

```rust
// In zonemap.rs
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Clone)]
struct ZoneMapStatistics {
    zone: ZoneMetadata,  // Common fields
    min: ScalarValue,
    max: ScalarValue,
    null_count: u32,
    nan_count: u32,
}

// In bloomfilter.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct BloomFilterStatistics {
    zone: ZoneMetadata,  // Common fields
    has_null: bool,
    bloom_filter: Sbbf,
}
```

## Alternative: Use a Trait for Shared Behavior

If you need shared methods, use a trait:

```rust
pub trait ZoneStatistics {
    fn zone_metadata(&self) -> &ZoneMetadata;
    fn fragment_id(&self) -> u64 {
        self.zone_metadata().fragment_id
    }
    fn zone_start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.zone_metadata().zone_start
    }
    fn zone_length(&self) -> usize {
        self.zone_metadata().zone_length
    }
}

impl ZoneStatistics for ZoneMapStatistics {
    fn zone_metadata(&self) -> &ZoneMetadata {
        &self.zone
    }
}

impl ZoneStatistics for BloomFilterStatistics {
    fn zone_metadata(&self) -> &ZoneMetadata {
        &self.zone
    }
}
```

## Benefits of This Approach

1. DRY: Common fields defined once
2. Type safety: Compile-time guarantees
3. Easy refactoring: Change common fields in one place
4. Clear intent: Shared metadata is explicit
5. No runtime overhead: Zero-cost abstraction

## Migration Path

1. Create `ZoneMetadata` in a shared location (e.g., `scalar/common.rs` or `scalar/mod.rs`)
2. Update both structs to use composition
3. Update access patterns: `stat.fragment_id` → `stat.zone.fragment_id` or add getter methods
4. Update serialization/deserialization code

Should I implement this refactoring? I can:
1. Create the shared `ZoneMetadata` struct
2. Update both `ZoneMapStatistics` and `BloomFilterStatistics`
3. Update all usages throughout the codebase
